title: When Safety Becomes an Attack Surface: Manipulating Abstention in Tool-Using AI Agents
abstract: arXiv:2611.14864v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: An AI agent's decision not to act can itself become an attack surface. We study warning-induced over-abstention, an availability attack in which adversaries place fabricated risk warnings in low-trust content to prevent legitimate task completion. Our central premise is that safe abstention requires evaluating both the claimed risk and the authority of the evidence supporting it. We develop controlled counterfactual task variants that vary risk content, source provenance, and warning wording, and evaluate a Verify-Before-Abstain protocol that corroborates warnings against authoritative records or the underlying content. Across three model families and 51 injectable AgentAbstain task pairs, caution-first prompting amplifies the attack. For Gemini, induced over-abstention rises from $9.8\%$ to $86.3\%$, despite unchanged clean-task completion. translated_title: 当安全成为攻击面：操纵工具使用型AI代理的弃权行为
translated_abstract: AI代理“不采取行动”的决定本身可能成为一种攻击面。我们研究了“警告诱发的过度弃权”，这是一种可用性攻击，攻击者在低信任度内容中放置伪造的风险警告，以阻止合法任务的完成。我们的核心前提是：安全的弃权需要同时评估所声称的风险本身以及支持该风险的证据的权威性。我们开发了受控的反事实任务变体，改变风险内容、来源出处和警告措辞，并评估了一种“先验证后弃权”协议，该协议通过权威记录或底层内容来核实警告的真实性。在三个模型系列和51个可注入的AgentAbstain任务对上的评估表明，“谨慎优先”的提示策略会放大这种攻击。对于Gemini模型，诱发的过度弃权从9.8%上升至86.3%，而干净任务的完成率保持不变。匹配措辞的对比实验进一步揭示了对警告语言的敏感性，并存在显著的……（摘要在此处截断）
tldr: 该论文揭示了AI代理的弃权机制本身可被武器化——攻击者只需在低信任内容中伪造风险警告即可诱导代理过度弃权、阻断合法任务完成，并提出“先验证后弃权”协议，通过核实警告来源的权威性来防御这种新型可用性攻击。
en_tdlr: This paper reveals that AI agents' abstention mechanisms can be weaponized—adversaries can fabricate risk warnings in low-trust content to induce over-abstention and block legitimate task completion—and proposes a Verify-Before-Abstain protocol that defends against this novel availability attack by verifying warning provenance against authoritative sources.
